newsitem.title: USA: Gold mining shares pounded in early U.S. activity.
newsitem.headline: Gold mining shares pounded in early U.S. activity.

text.p: Shares in gold mining tumbled in early U.S. trading on Monday as gold prices extended their recent slide and collapsed to 12-year lows.
Precious metals miners were by far the worst performing stocks among U.S.-listed equities. Canada-based Barrick Gold Corp fell 2-7/16 or 11 percent to 19-1/2 on
Other decliners included Newmont Mining Corp, down
2-1/4 to 35-5/8, Homestake Mining Co, off 5/8 to 12-3/8 and Placer Dome Inc, off 2-1/8 to 14-1/16 and
the NYSE's most active issue with 2.0 million shares traded.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Gold and Silver index skidded 8.37 points or nine percent at 86.33.
Gold prices, which have fallen steadily since the start of the year, received a new blow when Australia's central bank disclosed it had sold off about 60 percent of its gold reserves.
The Australian central bank divestitures followed recent sales by several European central banks and sent gold prices sliding through key support levels.
While sentiment has clearly turned against the group for the time being, some on Wall Street are still convinced that mining shares offer an opportunity for the patient.

"I'm still positive on them," said Oppenheimer & Co analyst Thomas McNamara. "What I would do is hold if I owned them; and if I was looking to buy, I'd wait on the sidelines just a little longer to see how bad it got."
McNamara said he would gravitate to "size and liquidity" when picking companies. Newmont Mining, the world's largest producer, is his top pick.

Assuming gold prices eventually turn around, he said, some larger companies will likely weather the price problems without much suffering because several have hedged production prices well into the future.
"If you look at a Barrick, for instance, they've locked in their forward production at about $420 per ounce," he said, with contracts running out for the next two years.
However, McNamara said investors should pick and choose carefully because "I think the industry as a whole is relatively under-hedged."
